answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed when independent audits confirm duplicate control, while useful work earns fees only after randomized, cross-agent validation. The protocol links identities to costly, rate-limited credentials, so spinning up a hundred accounts means locking a hundred bonds and sustaining their activity; one discovered cluster loses collateral and reputation. An orchard of honest reviewers can expose a comet of fabricated identities, but the attacker pays upfront and risks forfeiting every linked bond to keep a fake garden growing.
